candidate.title: BSAS
candidate.scope: The single BSAS (Bisulfite Amplicon Sequencing) row of the supplied Illumina poster: targeted amplification of bisulfite-converted genomic DNA followed by transposome-mediated sequencing-library construction. Masser et al. (2013), PMID 24279302, resolves the Nextera XT implementation and the unlabeled final library transition. The upper RRBS/scRRBS row, cropped BSPP labels, lower Methyl-Seq/MRE-Seq row, and right-hand UDP-glucose structure are neighboring context with no arrows into BSAS. Nextera XT is a library-preparation component, not an additional target method. The diagram ends at DNA; sequencing and methylation counting are described only to interpret that product.

states.label: DNA: completed sequencing library
features: Poster endpoint: four parallel blue lines labeled DNA after an unlabeled arrow; exact end structures and indexes are not drawn.

Primary-supported implementation: amplified library fragments with random inserts from the targeted bisulfite-PCR products, sequencing interface sequences (called capture probes in paper Figure 1), and dual sample indexes. Capture probes here are part of the final library description, not evidence for an additional target-capture operation.

The sequenced carrier is DNA copied from the converted target regions. C/T representation at covered CpG sites supports a methylation fraction across sampled reads, not whole-genome coverage or direct methyl-group detection.
Sample indexes allow reads from multiplexed libraries to be assigned back to a sample; pooling and sequencing are outside the depicted endpoint.

Bisulfite-derived signals may include both 5-mC and 5-hmC. The primary paper also notes possible target-PCR/tagmentation bias and reduced coverage near amplicon ends; random inserts do not ensure uniform or perfect representation.

operations.label: Bisulfite conversion
operations.description: Convert genomic DNA to bisulfite-treated DNA in which originally unmodified cytosines become uracils while methylated cytosines can remain cytosines.
operations.mechanism: Sodium-bisulfite treatment deaminates unmethylated cytosines to uracils; methylated cytosines resist conversion in the reported assay.
operations.information_effect: Transfers cytosine modification information into differential susceptibility to conversion. Standard BSAS does not distinguish 5-mC from 5-hmC.

operations.label: PCR with primers specific for bisulfite converted DNA
operations.description: Amplify chosen loci from bisulfite-converted genomic DNA with converted-sequence-specific primers, producing double-stranded target amplicons.
operations.mechanism: Bisulfite-specific PCR enriches target sequences and copies uracils as thymines while retained cytosines are represented as cytosines.
operations.information_effect: Primer-defined target selection limits the genomic regions represented. The amplified sequence, rather than persistence of original methyl groups, carries the readout as C/T differences.

operations.label: Tagmentation
operations.description: Act on the bisulfite-PCR amplicons with the adaptor-bearing transposome, producing fragmented amplicon-derived DNA tagged with adaptor segments.
operations.mechanism: Transposome-mediated simultaneous DNA fragmentation and adaptor attachment, termed tagmentation in the primary paper; implemented using Nextera XT.
operations.information_effect: Creates sequencing-library insert fragments from the selected amplicons while retaining their conversion-derived nucleotide information. The complex supplies adaptor material and catalytic activity; it is not a second biological sample.
